problem: The lead says the isotherm answers 'for a given feed concentration, how much solute will a gram hold'. Loading is set by the concentration left in the liquid at equilibrium, not by the feed concentration. A student may plug the feed value straight into q = qmax K_L C/(1 + K_L C) and oversize or undersize the carbon dose.
fix: Write: it answers, for a given equilibrium liquid concentration, how much solute one gram of carbon, silica or resin holds. Getting from a feed to that equilibrium value needs a mass balance.

where: Section 1, text after the C/q formula
problem: 'Divide intercept into 1/q_max to get K_L' can be read two ways; a student may divide the intercept by 1/q_max, which gives 1/K_L instead of K_L.
fix: Write: take 1/q_max and divide it by the intercept to get K_L, that is K_L = (1/q_max) ÷ intercept.

problem: The 'where:' clause of each displayed formula ends with plotting instructions ('Plot C/q against C: slope = ...'), which repeat the sentence just below and read like part of the symbol list.
fix: Keep only symbol definitions after 'where:' (q, C, q_max, K_L) and let the separate sentence carry the slope and intercept.

problem: n is called the heterogeneity index and then said to describe 'how steeply loading rises with concentration'. The steepness of the log-log line is 1/n, not n; calling n the steepness measure invites a student to read the slope as n.
fix: Say: n is the heterogeneity index; 1/n is the slope of the log q versus log C line, so a larger n means a flatter line and loading that rises more slowly with C.
